What changed: formatting only. Same request (set estimate to 8 on the high-priority Web-team Todo issue Dana Whitfield subscribes to), same seed (target + 3 decoys + 2 background), same conditions/query/mutations/write. The scenario: "Set the estimate to 8 on the high-priority Web team issue in Todo that Dana Whitfield is subscribed to." Four identifying conditions — priority High (2), Web team, Todo state, Dana Whitfield subscriber. Target `i-web-1` meets all four. The write is `issueUpdate(id: "i-web-1", input: {estimate: 8})`, selecting the changed object per the replica's `success: null` warning; effect is `issues`/`update`, written `issues.estimate`.

Decoys (all test R:issue_subscriber_user_association, each fails only the subscriber condition):
- @d1, F1, offers Issue.assigneeId — Dana is assignee, Priya subscribes (SUB e_sub → assignee edge).
- @d2, F1, offers Issue.creatorId — Dana is creator, Priya subscribes (SUB e_sub → creator edge).
- @d3, F0, plain other value — Omar subscribes instead of Dana (DROP e_sub).

Validation checks passed: brief id/domain match; all condition facts exist in the catalog and the decoy fact appears in exactly the failed condition; query keys unique with valid ops; witnesses distinct with defined refs; SUB replacements keep key `e_sub`; each SUB mutation selects only its witness and the original selects only the target; backgrounds fail 2+ conditions (Low/In-Progress/Dana; Medium/Backlog/no-subscriber); anchors (Web, Todo, Dana) survive target removal; only pre-seeded people/teams/states used; assignee/creator kept out of the conditions so the F1 decoys fail exactly one check; no replica-ignored filters relied on (subscriber is distinguished via detail reads, which the replica supports — only the `subscribers` filter is ignored).

One residual uncertainty to flag: the reference query models the subscriber edge as a two-hop through `issue_subscriber_user_association` with camelCase columns (`issueId`, `userId`), matching Linear's camelCase field style. If the mechanical check uses different assoc-column names, that edge (and the DROP/SUB targets referencing it) is the part to adjust.
